To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amphiphilic block conetworks composed from BMA, GMMA and EDMA are suitable materials for tissue engineering applications.
amphiphilic terpolymers of BMA/GMMA/EDMA are capable of forming conetworks with different surface compositions and that these have different cell adhesion properties and protein adsorption.

amphiphilic block conetworks composed from poly(butylmethacrylate-block-2,3 propendiol-1-methylacrylate-stat ethandiol dimethylacrylate) support cell proliferation and that the protein adsorption is dependent on the synthesis route.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and characterisation of amphiphilic terpolymer connetworks with the potential to be used as substrates for cell culture.
the development of new amphiphilic block conetworks that can be tailored to have different cell adhesion properties.
the synthesis and characterization of amphiphilic block conetworks composed mainly of butyl methyacrylate and 2,3-propandiol-1- methacrylate and ethandiol-dimethacrylate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GMMA class of block conetworks have a higher surface concentration of carboxylic acids and therefore are more hydrophilic than the GMAc class.
the GMMA conetworks are the best substrates for cell growth.
the block conetworks are suitable for use as cell culture substrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GMMA conetworks support cell viability and proliferation and that the GMAc conetworks support protein adsorption.
the GMMA networks are better for cell growth than the GMAc networks, and that the GMAc network is better for protein adsorption than the GMMA network.
the block conetworks with GMMA are the best for cell proliferation and the best for protein adsorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to control the surface chemistry of a material by the choice of monomer and the synthetic route.
it is possible to tune the surface composition and protein adsorption behaviour of block terpolymer networks.
the surface chemistry of the conetwork is a major factor that influences cell adhesion and proliferation.
